case.title: Fabricator keeps a fake participant on its own phone except for one slip months later

submissions.open_text: The community borehole committee collects fees but the pump handle is still broken.
Livestock drink upstream so river water is muddy during the dry season.
Tap water point opens at six and closes before noon most days.
We buy from the handcart man when the nearby tap is dry.
After the new connection our household saves time every morning.

case.why: An enumerator running a fake participant account keeps it on a separate phone (dev-p02) so the two logins never look linked, but slips once. q3 is a P02 submission made on E02's phone dev-n2, over five months after e1. dev-n2 therefore has 2 distinct contributors (E02, P02), and the rule counts submissions at any time, before or after, so e1 must fire. Several wrong implementations would let the fabricator through: one that limits the lookup to a time window around the submission; one that only considers earlier submissions, since q3 is later than e1; one that requires each contributor to have several submissions on the device; and one that assigns each device to its majority user and ignores minority contributors. The other checks stay quiet for e1: E02's submissions are on different days, all points are inside Nyalenda, e1 is a daytime interview of 1490 s, and its transcript is empty.
